mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (measured as the 3-month change in FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary easing supports risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1 percentage points over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 9.5% signals severe labor market distress, triggering risk-off sentiment that depresses equity valuations through reduced consumer spending and corporate revenue expectations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 9.5% for at least 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% over the prior 3 months indicates weakening consumer demand, reducing corporate revenue expectations and triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS decline > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline by more than 0.5% over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production contraction (INDPRO decline > 0.5% over 3 months) signals deteriorating manufacturing output, reducing corporate profit margins and triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.2% over the prior 3 months indicates strengthening labor market conditions, boosting consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS increases by at least 0.2% over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth below 12900 billion (GDPC1 < 12900) indicates economic contraction, reducing corporate earnings expectations and triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 is below 12900, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in CPI (CPIAUCSL > 0.2% over 3 months) and stable/falling FEDFUNDS above 0.15% indicates monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.2% and FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.15% over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary easing cycle (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%), accommodative policy reduces discount rates for equity valuation, supporting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through enhanced risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
